title: How long do porcelain veneers last, and what makes them fail?
seoTitle: How Long Do Porcelain Veneers Last? 10-Year Data, Why They Fail
description: Porcelain veneers last 10 to 15 years; 95.5% survive 10 years and 91% 20 years. How they fail, why the first two years matter, and what a 5-year warranty means.
author: Dr. Roger Ramos Navarro, DMD
imageAlt: Ceramist hand-finishing a porcelain veneer in the Xiluet Smiles lab
answer: With normal care, porcelain veneers last **10 to 15 years**, and often longer. Pooled data on 6,500 veneers shows **95.5% still in place at 10 years**; one long-term study found **91% at 20 years**. When veneers fail, it is usually a fracture or a veneer coming loose, most often in the first two years. At Xiluet Smiles, every veneer carries a 5-year written warranty.

sections.h2: What the data says about veneer lifespan

blocks.p: The number most dentists give is 10 to 15 years. The research supports it. A [pooled analysis of 6,500 porcelain veneers from 25 clinical studies](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7961608/) found an estimated 10-year survival of 95.5%, counting fracture, debonding, decay and root canal treatment all as failures. A long-term study by Layton and Walton of porcelain veneers bonded to enamel reported [96% survival at 10 years and 91% at 20 years](https://www.aesthetic-dentistry.com/longevity-porcelain-veneers).

Survival means the veneer is still in place and working, not that it looks exactly as it did the day it was bonded. Porcelain does not stain or wear the way composite does, so a 12-year-old porcelain veneer usually still looks good. Composite veneers, by contrast, typically last [5 to 7 years](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/23522-dental-veneers) before they need repair or replacement.

Two caveats. Data beyond 20 years is thin, because modern bonding has not been in use much longer than that. And averages hide a wide spread: a veneer on a non-grinder with good hygiene can outlast the numbers, while a veneer on an untreated grinder can fail in its first year.

In the pooled study, the two leading complications were fracture (154 cases) and debonding, the veneer coming off in one piece (85 cases). Decay under the margin (8 cases) and teeth needing root canals (16 cases) were rare. Most failures happened early, within about two years of bonding. A veneer that survives its first two years has passed the hardest test.

blocks.p: Figures are from the [same pooled analysis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7961608/). The lesson is in the right-hand column: three of the four failure modes are decided by how the veneer is planned and bonded, before you ever eat with it.

sections.h2: The five things that shorten a veneer's life

steps: **Grinding and clenching.** Porcelain is strong under compression and weak under bending. Night-time grinding puts bending forces on the edges, hour after hour. It is the single biggest reason for chips.

**Bonding to dentin instead of enamel.** In a 15-year study of [672 veneers](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jerd.70016), dentin exposure raised the odds of failure about 3.5 times. Thin, conservative preparation keeps the bond on enamel.
**Using your teeth as tools.** Ice, nutshells, pens, opening packages, biting fingernails. Porcelain copes with eating. It does not cope with impact.
**A bite that was never checked.** If one veneer edge hits first when you close or slide sideways, it takes all the force. The bite is adjusted at delivery and checked again if anything feels high.
**Neglected margins.** The porcelain cannot decay, but the tooth at its edge can. Brushing, flossing and a cleaning every six months protect the margin.

blocks.p: Design matters too. The pooled data found that veneers covering the biting edge outperformed those that stopped short of it, and that newer pressed porcelains outperformed older feldspathic ones. Choices like these are made by your doctor and ceramist together, usually without you noticing, which is one more reason to ask who the ceramist is and where they work.

sections.h2: If you grind, get the night guard

blocks.p: During the day your veneers meet the forces they were designed for: chewing, speaking, the occasional apple. At night, a grinder can apply far more force for far longer with no awareness of it. A night guard is a thin custom splint that takes that load instead of the porcelain. We recommend one for every patient who grinds, and your doctor will usually see the signs at Visit 1: flattened edges, wear facets, a tight jaw in the morning. Clenching without grinding counts too; it loads the front teeth more than most people expect.

For a grinder, a night guard is not optional. It is the difference between veneers that last 15 years and veneers that chip in the first one. Under our warranty, normal care and wearing the guard if you grind are expected. Ask for the written terms.

sections.h2: What the 5-year written warranty actually means

blocks.p: Most Miami practices whose published offers we checked in October 2026 gave no warranty on veneers; the longest we found was 1 year. Ours is 5 years, in writing, and we hand you the document at Visit 3, the day your veneers are bonded. It covers the veneer. Normal care, regular cleanings and a night guard if you grind are expected. Ask for the written terms before you book, and keep them.

Five years is possible for a practical reason: our ceramist works in the same building as the doctors. If a veneer chips, the doctor who placed it looks at it, and the ceramist who made it remakes it, with the original design and shade on file. There is no outside lab to ship to and no second clinic to argue with. For out-of-town patients, the clinic is 15 minutes from Miami International Airport.

Put the warranty next to the lifespan data and the logic is clear. The years when failure is most likely are the first two. A 5-year warranty covers those years with margin to spare. After that, the data says your veneers are in a long, stable stretch. Read more on [what a veneer warranty should cover](/blog/veneer-warranty-what-it-covers).

sections.h2: What to do if a veneer chips or comes off

steps: **Keep the piece.** A veneer that comes off whole can often be rebonded as it is, if it is intact and nobody has tried to glue it.
**Do not use superglue or a pharmacy repair kit.** It contaminates the surface and can make rebonding impossible.
**Call us the same day.** In the first years this is a warranty matter, and we want to see it.
**If you are out of town, send a photo.** The doctor will tell you whether it can wait for your next visit or needs attention locally.

blocks.quote: A veneer that fails in the first two years was usually a planning problem, not a patient problem. That is why the warranty is ours to carry, not yours.

blocks.p: Lifespan starts with design. If you are comparing offers, ask each practice how much enamel it will remove, whether the ceramist is in the building, and what the warranty says in writing. Then send photos to our [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation) and compare. See also [whether veneers ruin your teeth](/blog/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth) and [what veneers cost in Miami](/blog/porcelain-veneers-cost-miami).

faq.q: How long do porcelain veneers last?
faq.a: With normal care, 10 to 15 years is typical. Pooled data on 6,500 veneers shows 95.5% survival at 10 years, and one long-term study found 91% at 20 years. Ours are covered for 5 years in writing.

faq.q: Do veneers need to be replaced eventually?
faq.a: Yes. Even a veneer that never chips will eventually be replaced because of wear, gum changes or a change in the neighbouring teeth. Plan for a replacement after 10 to 20 years; it is a similar procedure to the first one.

faq.q: Can a chipped veneer be repaired?
faq.a: Small chips can often be polished or repaired with composite. Larger fractures mean a new veneer. Because our ceramist is in the building and your design is on file, a remake matches the original.

Porcelain itself does not stain. The natural tooth at the margin can, and so can the cement line over many years, which is why cleanings matter. Composite veneers do stain, which is one reason they last about half as long.

faq.q: What does the Xiluet warranty cover?
faq.a: The veneer, for 5 years, in writing, handed to you at Visit 3. Normal care, regular cleanings and a night guard if you grind are expected. Ask for the written terms before you book.

faq.q: How long do composite veneers last?
faq.a: About 5 to 7 years before they need repair or replacement, compared with 10 to 15 for porcelain. They cost less up front and more per year.
